prompt:
feat(projection): narrow a stack profile to the files it applies to (S50, ADR-071)

A stack profile was always-on everywhere, because profiles reached a
reader through the generated region in AGENTS.md and through nothing else.
A profile can now declare simt-scope, and a repository on Cursor, Copilot
or Antigravity gets it as a file the surface attaches on patterns instead
of one every agent loads on every request.

The narrowing happens only when EVERY selected surface can do it. Claude
Code's paths key is documented and silently fails to lazy-load for quoted
values, and opencode has no per-rule channel at all, so a repository
carrying either keeps its profiles in the region and is told which surface
stopped it. That ruling is the reason decision 3 in surfaces.mjs still
stands, and this row cross-references it rather than re-opening it: a rule
that never loads is worse than one that loads eagerly.

Reading the two vendors' own docs changed the design before any code did.
Antigravity requires patterns starting with * to be quoted, because an
unquoted one is a YAML alias anchor and the rule is discarded with no
message at all, and it documents a 20,000-token budget for always_on rules
past which they are demoted to pointers, so an eager profile costs the
reader a budget rather than merely wasting space. Cursor documents no
description plus no globs as manual mention only, so a scoped rule that
carried neither would never attach.

A simt-scope matching everything is refused rather than honoured: ** and *
are what a surface applies when given no pattern, so the profile would
be eager with a narrowing-looking spelling. Scoped files go through the
existing ruleTargets construction and are gated by checkTargets, so a file
this tool wrote is a file the gate can report drift on.
f2p: a profile is only narrowed by a surface, never by a bare key the reader would see
a quoted pattern is read as the pattern, not as the quotes around it
a scope that matches everything is refused, because it is not narrowing
a scoped file is gated like any other: drift and absence both fail the check
a scoped profile leaves the region for the surfaces that can narrow it
a surface that cannot narrow keeps the profile in the region, and says why
an eager rule still emits no scoping frontmatter (decision 3)
an empty scope is refused too
an unscoped profile behaves exactly as it did before
every key the scoped shape emits is in the vendor docs, checked on both shapes
every shipped profile that declares a scope has patterns that narrow
only surfaces whose scoping key was read in the vendor docs can narrow
the scoped file carries the patterns the surface was documented to take
p2p: a backend Workers repo does not receive the React profile
a malformed region is refused rather than duplicated
a region past a reader limit is reported, and place top clears it
a rendered region steps headings by one and gives each source one heading
a repo with no detectable signal still gets the shared rules
a surface problem is reported in `surfaceProblems`, not in `mdcProblems`
check reports current, drift, unmanaged and absent distinctly
every rule applies-to tag is one fingerprint can emit as a tag or a fact
every rule file carries an id
render strips frontmatter and the duplicated H1
selection is core plus intersecting profiles, in a stable order
sync never touches hand-written content outside the markers
the fallback profile is only chosen when nothing more specific matched
the region records the simt-dev sha so drift is diagnosable
